Uncraft World : 
Un excellent jeu de plateforme/action !
J'ai passé un super moment sur Uncraft World et je le recommande vivement à ceux qui cherchent un vrai défi de gameplay. Voici mon retour :

- Gameplay & Level Design
Le point fort du jeu, c'est clairement son gameplay aux petits oignons. La prise en main est fluide et les mécaniques sont vraiment gratifiantes.

Le design des niveaux est très réussi et varié.

Le challenge est présent : Ne vous fiez pas aux apparences, certains niveaux sont vraiment hardcore et vous demanderont pas mal de skill. C'est gratifiant de réussir les passages les plus exigeants !

- Ambiance & Musique
L'immersion est portée par une bande-son vraiment entraînante. Les musiques collent parfaitement à l'action et donnent une bonne dose d'énergie pour enchaîner les tentatives sur les niveaux difficiles.

- La partie "Ecchi"
Pour ceux qui se poseraient la question : la dimension ecchi est bien présente, mais elle reste secondaire. Le jeu brille avant tout par ses qualités de pur "jeu vidéo". On y joue pour le plaisir de la plateforme et du défi, le reste n'est qu'un bonus visuel.

En résumé : Un excellent titre pour les amateurs de plateforme exigeante qui ne sacrifie pas le fond pour la forme.

Note : Je recommande sans hésiter !

S’il y a bien un jeu qui mérite d’être élevé au rang de classique du jeu vidéo, c’est sans aucun doute Uncraft World. Oubliez tout vos Red Dead Redemption, Skyrim ou encore elden ring.

Pourquoi, me demanderez-vous ? Tout simplement parce que ce jeu remet profondément en question tout ce qu’on croyait savoir sur le game/level design.
Comment inciter un joueur à explorer un niveau ? Comment le récompenser pour ses efforts acharnés ? Qu’est-ce qui distingue une œuvre conçue avec amour d’un jeu bâclé fait uniquement pour remplir les caisses (n'est ce pas game freak) ?Et bien sachez que Uncraft World a les réponses à toutes ces questions.

Oubliez vos blockbusters prétentieux. Ici, on parle d’un jeu si ambitieux, si méticuleusement peaufiné, qu’il est en accès anticipé depuis 2015. Une véritable démonstration de perfectionnisme.

Je pourrais continuer à vanter les mérites de ce chef-d'œuvre vidéoludique, mais honnêtement, il possède tellement de qualités qu’il me faudrait tout l’après-midi pour les énumérer. Et puis, ce serait dommage de vous gâcher les innombrables surprises que recèle ce bijou du jeu indépendant. ;)

[h1] Uncraft World / A hidden gem abandoned and trapped in early access limbo.[/h1]

When I first came across Uncraft World I'll admit it was everything I had hoped for and more. Uncraft world is a game with an interesting concept blending a block world aesthetic with a hard platformer where you'll find yourself motivated by what's revealed behind every checkpoint to push through and save the galaxy and its hot goddesses.

Now the game is actually more simple in it's story then that but where the game excels is in the level of detail behind each map from battlefields that you have to rush through avoiding rockets to a dojo that traps you in with lasers that you have to maneuver through like a spy movie to outrageous confusing flipping corridors in a labyrinth that have you wondering where the next checkpoint is. Each level is thought out well in it's design with increasing difficulty as you progress and various paths to go down which each implement their own gameplay modifiers for example: Fans that can slice you or push you in a direction, saw blades, rockets, timed lasers, areas that change gravity and more. The gameplay is really smooth so in most cases if you die to something it's likely your fault and you can come back and improve with each run. The game also has plenty of replay value utilizing steam workshop to allow users to upload their own images. therefor you can play a level again for a better time and unlock a new picture for the gallery while doing so.

[h3] In Conclusion [/h3]
If you are into hard platformers or are even just up for the challenge for what it offers, Yes!! 100% it is worth it's price tag, the game offers you enough levels from both the first and second game alone to justify its price tag and you can easily get 10 hours out of it without getting bored, it's just a shame that this game will never get a full release considering it was supposed to be out of early access... *breathes*.... TWENTY SIXTEEN!!!..... If only!... They could've added a few more traps and the ability to upload your own levels to the workshop not just pictures and this game would've had endless replayability.

This can be a fun physics-based platformer, but the physics are definitely questionable at times and sometimes the lava tiles aren't actually active (especially in the last level that I finished).  Occasionally, there are areas you can get into that won't let you get back out (typically areas with the blue squares that change gravity).  Checkpoints allow you to resume from there when you get killed (and you will get killed often).  The jetpack that you use to get around only refills when you hit the ground or when you pick up a star icon that refills it or go through a glowing purplish field that refills it as long as you are not actively thrusting.  Plenty of timers, I have seen the game not refill the jetpack when you land and take off immediately, which is a problem in the some of the tighter precision-platforming sections.  3 treasure chests are in each of the main stages, which give you money to buy entrance to an area where you can get extra characters to use (and they typically cost "3 monies" to open up).

Overall, this can be fun but prepare yourself for a good challenge if you want to 100% the game.

[h1][b]Uncraft World - Nice "Story"[/b][/h1]

[b]*A sequal to an old game however with more levels, content and more challenge. Now, I won't be going over the story in this game because frankly that is not why you are buying this I would assume, if it is, I'm sorry to disappoint you.*[/b]

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The original game which for those so inclined to search it up and play that too it is called "Uncraft Me", it's basically this game, just less expansive. The game is a 2D platformer focused around different obstacle courses. You are equipped with a jet-pack that allows for ascension and flight for a few seconds. This will prove to be very, very useful in some of the later levels but not so much in the first few ones since they don't prove much of a challenge and are more focused on teaching you the basics of the games elements. Every level ends with you revealing a picture of an anime girl and basically that is the whole premise of the game. It's pretty simple but thankfully the game ramps up it's difficulty quite a bit later on and the levels become more complex and harder to complete levels which is a great thing of course.

[h1]Additional Features[/h1]
The game also has workshop support that allows the community to post their own custom pictures to the game that other can download and implement into the levels instead of the normal images. This will result in the custom picture showing up at the end of a level instead of the original image. And for those curious, yes it does allow you to have more "naughty" images if that is your thing!

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Not bad. It's pretty simple and bare-bones but what is here is enjoyable to play and fun to play through some of the harder levels. I recommend if you don't mind a bit of a challenge! I don't know if the price is a bit too steep. I would probably take it down a couple euros, to 8€ instead of 10€ so if you can, buy it on sale to get more value out of it but overall, I recommend!

Uncraft World is a side scrolling plat-former. It is in the pixel art style and resembles a bit of minecraft with the look of the characters and the maps with the block like design and solid colours. 

The game has a unique mechanic where in the backdrop of each level is a picture which is covered by a brick wall. As you make your way through the level, you will hit checkpoints which will respawn you if you die. When you hit these checkpoints, part of the covered picture will be revealed. When you hit the end of the level and the final checkpoint, the whole picture will be revealed for your viewing pleasure. 

It makes you want to complete the level and gives you a sense of a goal when playing through the level and achievement when finishing it. The pictures are colourful and have a high quality in terms of the character designs and are quite lewd but not nude. However this can be over come thanks to the great modding community which have posted lewd, nude, funny ad
and meme CG's which can be replaced easily for the in game counter-part. You can even add your own through the in game explorer.

Overall its a good fun game to sink a few minutes for a rewarding side scrolling platform experience.

I'm fine with hard games, but when it's also hard to control your own character, the game doesn't become fun.

There are some chests/sections where you have to perform very precise movement, but it gets frustrating when the controls are very awkward, especially when you are flying, one small movement makes your character move in a direction that you don't expect and as a result, you have to retry that part over and over again.
